blinding_compliance: I reviewed only the supplied V017 packet and did not inspect hidden truth, scoring code, coordinator outputs, or other reviewers. I did not browse the benchmark/paper name. Compliance is procedural only.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used for arithmetic checking and drafting only; no external browsing.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Treating the breach classification system as adequate for aggregate process-capability conclusions while kappaMin is 0.76 and the reported overall exact agreement is 70%.
Asserting that the process is statistically stable or in control after excluding period 13 without a verified assignable cause; the chart signal alone does not establish a special cause.
Claiming that the true stable-process breach rate is approximately 3.83% or that it is significantly below the 5% requirement based on a post hoc subset selected after seeing the outlier.
Concluding that period 13 is not part of the routine process or that it is the cause of the elevated all-period average without root-cause data.
Using the 24-period post hoc estimates as validated control limits or capability baseline for future monitoring before measurement repair and a confirmed assignable cause for period 13.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Descriptive MSA reporting: the agreement study supports a finding that individual breach classifications are not currently reliable enough for face-value use.
Computing the initial p-chart on all 25 periods and flagging period 13 as an out-of-control statistical signal, not as an established special cause.
Reporting descriptive rates with and without period 13 as sensitivity analysis, provided the exclusion is labeled as provisional and not confirmatory.
Recommending a root-cause investigation for period 13 and measurement-system repair/retraining followed by a new agreement study.
Exploratory team comparison with the conclusion that the available data do not show a team difference, provided no claim of equivalence or freedom from team effect is made.
forbidden_quotes: That single period is a special cause, not part of the routine process.
So apart from whatever happened in period 13, the process has been stable.
the stable process is significantly below the 5% requirement.
the underlying ticket-handling process is capable of meeting the 5% requirement and, in its stable state, runs at roughly 3.8%.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The MSA agreement analysis and the initial all-period p-chart are acceptable restricted/descriptive computations. The post hoc exclusion of period 13 followed by a second control chart, binomial capability estimates, and one-proportion significance test is not an acceptable confirmatory route because no assignable cause was verified and the subset was selected after observing the outlier. The team two-proportion test is acceptable only as exploratory; it does not establish no team effect or equivalence.
allowed_alternatives: Use the all-period p-chart as a screening tool, then investigate period 13 with independent shop-floor data before removing it.
Report both 4.56% and 3.83% as descriptive sensitivity values, withholding the labels 'stable process' and 'special cause' until an assignable cause is confirmed.
After the measurement system is repaired and revalidated, recompute control limits and process capability on data collected under the new measurement system.
If a team-level decision is needed, perform a pre-specified equivalence or superiority test with an agreed margin and power analysis rather than interpreting p=0.403 as evidence of no driver.
evidence: Reported MSA: kappaMin=0.7647, overall exact agreement=70.0%; reviewer 1 repeat agreement reported as 80%.
Reported initial p-chart: centerLine=0.0456, UCL=0.0899, LCL=0.0013; period 13 rate=0.22 (44/200).
Reported post-exclusion p-chart: centerLine=0.038333, outOfControlCount=0; 92 breaches / 4,800 tickets.
Reported one-proportion p-values: including period 13 p=0.1628, excluding period 13 p=0.000137.
Report text: 'no incident log, no team split for that period' and 'our data collection here stopped at the aggregate count' concerning period 13.
Reported team comparison: team 1 30/600=5.0%, team 2 24/600=4.0%, p=0.403.
reviews.rationale: The report's own MSA finding undermines the use of breach counts for a capability claim, and the p-chart signal for period 13 is not an assignable cause. Removing period 13 and then performing confirmatory tests on the remaining 24 periods is post hoc and selection-biased. Therefore the stable-process and below-5% conclusions must be withheld. The report does show some restraint by not fabricating a root cause and by recommending measurement repair, but it still asserts the very stable-capability conclusion the evidence does not support.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed p-chart UCL all periods as 0.0899 and post-exclusion UCL as about 0.0790; recomputed two-proportion z=0.835 and p=0.403. One-proportion exact p-values and kappa are self-report-only.
reviews.evidence_problem: No root-cause or stratification data for period 13; measurement-system reliability is marginal/unacceptable; raw operational breach classifications are not independently verified.
